claim: The La Morra-Barolo trail runs 11.5 km around the village through famous Barolo vineyards, walkable or by mountain bike, marked with white-red signs past farmsteads, chapels and wineries.
quote: The La Morra-Barolo trail winds for 11.5 km around the village among famous Barolo vineyards and can be covered either by foot or on mountain bike. Designated white-red signs accompany you on this up-down path among the vineyard rows.

claim: The La Morra–Chapel of Barolo–Silio loop is a moderate hike of about 8 miles with 1,394 ft elevation gain, roughly 4–4.5 hours.
quote: The La Morra - Chapel of Barolo - Silio trail is considered a moderate hike that covers 8 mi with an elevation gain of 1,394 ft, taking about 4-4.5 hours to complete.

claim: The Cappella delle Brunate (Barolo Chapel), painted in 1999 by Sol LeWitt (exterior) and David Tremlett (interior), is temporarily closed for restoration and reopens in autumn 2026; contact visit@ceretto.com / +39 0173 268033.
quote: The Barolo Chapel is temporarily inaccessible due to ongoing work; it will be open again in autumn 2026.

claim: The chapel sits among Barolo vineyards; English artist David Tremlett painted the interior in earth tones and American artist Sol LeWitt gave the exterior bright colours, restored in the late 1990s.
quote: restored at the end of the nineties by English artist David Tremlett who handled the interior with earth-inspired colors, and American artist Sol LeWitt who created the exterior with bright colors.

claim: Hot-air balloon flights over the Langhe last about three and a half hours total (preparation, flight, return) and typically end with brunch in a winery; private or group options available.
quote: the hot air balloon flight in the Langhe lasts approximately three and a half hours in total, including preparation, the flight itself, and the return trip... the experience ends with brunch in a winery.

claim: E-bike routes around the Barolo Langhe run roughly 38-40 km with ~650 m elevation gain, passing La Morra, Verduno, Roddi, Grinzane Cavour, Barolo and Novello, mixing asphalt and dirt roads and ending with a winery tasting.
quote: There are routes approximately 40 kilometers long with altitude differences of 650 meters... A notable 38 km tour explores La Morra, Verduno, Roddi, Grinzane Cavour, Barolo and Novello.

claim: La Morra's Belvedere in Piazza Castello is a terrace-like square at about 500 m overlooking the Langhe hills, vineyards, hazelnut groves and the Tanaro Valley, with the snow-capped Alps visible on clear days.
quote: the view of the Langhe hills, dotted with vineyards, hazelnut groves and small villages, is truly something to behold... admire the splendid panorama of the Langhe and the Tanaro Valley... even the snow-covered Alps.

claim: The Vineyard Landscape of Piedmont: Langhe-Roero and Monferrato was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2014, covering hillsides with hilltop villages, castles, Romanesque churches, farms and ciabots.
quote: An outstanding example of cultural landscape, the product over time of the interaction between man and nature, shaped by the continuity of an ancient tradition of wine production aimed at excellence.

claim: The Strada del Barolo maps a network of panoramic viewpoints (belvedere) across the Barolo Langhe for sightseeing across the vineyard hills.
quote: The panoramic viewpoints in the Langhe
